summary: kiln-pool pods are shared mutable state — once leased, any pre-existing scripts on the pod (other lab bootstraps, autonomous loops) can also acquire/restart kiln serve, causing mid-eval HTTP 500 / RemoteDisconnected for the new lessee. On this pod, the pi-compaction-grpo v062 autonomous loop's startup script restarted kiln serve mid-iter0-eval and 4/23 tasks errored. There's no isolation mechanism between concurrent agents sharing a pod's filesystem + kiln-serve singleton.
repro_hint: Acquire any kiln-pool H100; ps -ef | grep -i pi-compaction may reveal another lab's bootstrap script still running. The kiln-serve binary itself is a singleton on port 8420 — only one process can bind it.

summary: cuda_grpo_ablation on pi-compaction-sized rollouts is prohibitively slow even with KILN_GRAD_CHECKPOINT_SEGMENTS=8: 4 strong-signal groups × ~30K tokens each = ~120K total token budget; full training step did not produce a single progress= line in 6 minutes on H100 SXM. Pi-doctest training (~150K total token budget over 11 groups) completed in 2-3 min on the same hardware. The 4x slowdown isn't strictly token-count proportional — long-sequence GDN backward pass dominates wall time and scales superlinearly.
repro_hint: Build a GrpoGroup with completions whose combined assistant-text + source-text is ~15-30K tokens each; submit to cuda_grpo_ablation phase1 with rank=16 lr=1e-5 KILN_GRAD_CHECKPOINT_SEGMENTS=8. Pi-doctest training data has ~3K tokens per group total, which is what kiln-train is tuned for.
